# Use a stable, recent base image suitable for HPC builds
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set DEBIAN_FRONTEND to noninteractive to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install essential build tools, dependencies, OpenMPI, and certificates
# Combine into a single layer to reduce image size
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git \
    wget \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce final image size
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments like Kubernetes
# This ensures MPI can run as root and uses TCP for inter-container communication
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
# Prioritize TCP over shared memory or high-speed interconnects not present in typical containers
ENV OMPI_MCA_pml=ob1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp
# Explicitly bind to the primary container network interface (usually eth0)
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0

# Clone, build, and install the Kripke application
# This is done in a single RUN command to optimize layer usage and clean up sources
RUN git clone --depth 1 --recurse-submodules -b master https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke && \
    cd /opt/kripke && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build for a CPU-only environment with MPI and OpenMP enabled
    cmake \
        -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
        -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
        -D ENABLE_OPENMP=ON \
        -D ENABLE_CUDA=OFF \
        -D ENABLE_HIP=OFF \
        .. && \
    # Build with all available processor cores
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Copy the final executable to a standard location on the system PATH
    # FIX: The compiled executable is named kripke.exe; copy it to /usr/local/bin/kripke.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Clean up the source and build directories to minimize final image size
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/kripke

# Set a default working directory
WORKDIR /

# Provide a default command to facilitate interactive use
CMD ["/bin/bash"]

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the Kripke HPC benchmark
# on a single AWS CPU-based instance within a Kubernetes cluster using the Flux Operator.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster-aws-cpu
  # The Kubernetes namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods to create for the MiniCluster. For a single-node job, this is set to 1.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks/ranks for the job. Flux will execute the command with `flux run -n 4 ...`.
  tasks: 4

  # Do not delete the pods and associated resources upon job completion.
  # This is useful for debugging and inspecting logs or output files.
  cleanup: false

  # Logging verbosity and behavior settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # When true, the operator will not allow the job to continue if there are any errors.
    strict: true

  # Defines the container(s) that will run as part of the MiniCluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to be executed by Flux. The operator prepends `flux run -n <tasks>`.
      # This specific command runs Kripke with parameters suitable for 4 tasks.
      command: kripke --procs 2,2,1 --niter 10 --zones 12,12,12 --groups 4
      # Per instructions, launcher is set to false.
      launcher: false

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest is designed to run the Kripke HPC benchmark
# on a single, powerful AWS Graviton (ARM) instance, maximizing performance.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster-aws-cpu
  # The Kubernetes namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods to create for the MiniCluster.
  # This job is constrained to a single, large node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks/ranks. This is set to utilize all 64
  # cores of the target hpc7g.16xlarge instance.
  tasks: 64

  # Pod spec modifications to ensure scheduling on the correct instance type.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # This selector targets a specific AWS EC2 instance type optimized for HPC workloads.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # Flux-specific configuration.
  flux:
    container:
      # The ARM-compatible Flux image is required for the target Graviton processor.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Do not delete the pod upon job completion to allow for debugging and log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # When true, the operator will not allow the job to continue if there are any errors.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container. There should only be one for this job.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The 'launcher' property is now omitted, which defaults to 'true'.
      # This is the critical fix: it instructs the Flux Operator to wrap the command
      # with 'flux run', correctly starting it as a multi-process MPI application.
      # The command is updated to a larger problem size suitable for 64 tasks
      # (4x4x4 decomposition), maximizing utilization of the target hardware.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --niter 20 --zones 24,24,24 --groups 4

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest resolves an "Exec format error" by targeting
# an amd64-based AWS instance, ensuring architecture compatibility for all components.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster-aws-cpu
  # The Kubernetes namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The job is constrained to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of MPI tasks is updated to 48 to match the vCPU count of the new target instance (c7a.12xlarge).
  tasks: 48

  # Pod spec modifications to ensure scheduling on the correct amd64 instance type.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # This selector targets a compute-optimized amd64 instance to resolve the previous architecture mismatch.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  # Do not delete the pod upon job completion to allow for debugging and log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # When true, the operator will not allow the job to continue if there are any errors.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command is updated for the new task count. The process decomposition
      # (4x4x3) now correctly multiplies to 48 tasks, matching the spec.tasks field.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,3 --niter 20 --zones 24,24,24 --groups 4
      # Note: The 'flux.container.image' for ARM is removed, allowing the operator
      # to use its default amd64-compatible Flux view, resolving the binary execution error.

# This corrected MiniCluster manifest addresses the previous job timeout by
# targeting a more powerful AWS Graviton (ARM) instance. This allows the same
# computationally intensive workload to complete within the time limit.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-minicluster-aws-cpu
  # The Kubernetes namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The job is constrained to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of MPI tasks is increased to 64 to utilize all cores of the powerful hpc7g.16xlarge instance.
  tasks: 64

  flux:
    container:
      # The ARM-compatible Flux image is required to run on the Graviton processor.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9

  # Pod spec modifications to schedule the job on the more powerful instance.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # This selector targets a specific ARM-based AWS EC2 instance optimized for HPC workloads.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge

  # Do not delete the pod upon job completion to allow for debugging and log inspection.
  cleanup: false
  # When true, the operator will not allow the job to continue if there are any errors.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Defines the application container.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command's process decomposition is updated to 4x4x4 to match the 64 tasks,
      # ensuring the application fully utilizes the upgraded hardware.
      command: kripke --procs 4,4,4 --niter 20 --zones 24,24,24 --groups 4

# This manifest corrects the previous "Unknown options --nthreads" error.
# The invalid command-line argument has been removed and replaced with the
# standard OMP_NUM_THREADS environment variable to control threading.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-minicluster-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Do not delete the pod upon job completion to allow for debugging.
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - # The command is corrected by removing the unsupported '--nthreads' flag.
    command: kripke --procs 4,3,2 --niter 20 --zones 32,32,32 --groups 4
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
    # The standard environment variable for OpenMP is now used to set the thread count.
    environment:
      OMP_NUM_THREADS: "2"
  # Enforce strict logging to fail the job on any operator errors.
  logging:
    strict: true
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      # The job continues to target a compute-optimized amd64 instance.
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge
  # The job is constrained to run on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The number of MPI tasks remains 24, matching the process decomposition (--procs 4,3,2).
  tasks: 24

# the number of zones is evenly divisible by the number of MPI processes in each dimension.

  name: kripke-minicluster-aws-cpu

spec:

  cleanup: false
  containers:
